romaji: Anata wa Nihongo no benkyou ga nagai desu ne.
english: You've been studying Japanese for a long time, haven't you?
exampleRomaji: Anata wa Nihongo no benkyou ga nagai desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: あなたは日(に)本(ほん)語(ご)の勉(べん)強(きょう)が長(なが)いですね。
exampleEn: You've been studying Japanese for a long time, haven't you?
audioPath: clips/001_あなたは日本語の勉強が長いですね。.wav
grammar2: 長(なが)い (long) ↔ 短(みじか)い (short)

romaji: Mou ni-nen benkyou shite imasu.
english: I've been studying for two years already.
exampleRomaji: Mou ni-nen benkyou shite imasu.
japaneseFurigana: もう二(に)年(ねん)勉強(べんきょう)しています。
exampleEn: I've been studying for two years already.
audioPath: clips/002_もう2年勉強しています。.wav
grammar2: 〜ています = running state

romaji: Kaiwa ga totemo jouzu ni narimashita ne.
english: Your conversation skills have become very good, haven't they?
exampleRomaji: Kaiwa ga totemo jouzu ni narimashita ne.
japaneseFurigana: 会話(かいわ)がとても上手(じょうず)になりましたね。
exampleEn: Your conversation skills have become very good, haven't they?
audioPath: clips/003_会話がとても上手になりましたね。.wav
grammar2: 上(じょう)手(ず) (skillful) ↔ 下(へ)手(た) (unskillful)

romaji: Arigatou gozaimasu.
english: Thank you very much.
exampleRomaji: Arigatou gozaimasu.
japaneseFurigana: ありがとうございます。
exampleEn: Thank you very much.
audioPath: clips/004_ありがとうございます。.wav

romaji: Demo, kanji wa mada muzukashii desu.
english: But kanji is still difficult for me.
exampleRomaji: Demo, kanji wa mada muzukashii desu.
japaneseFurigana: でも、漢字(かんじ)はまだ難(むずか)しいです。
exampleEn: But kanji is still difficult for me.
audioPath: clips/005_でも漢字はまだ難しいです。.wav
grammar2: 難(むずか)しい (difficult) ↔ 優(やさ)しい (easy)

romaji: Mainichi dono kurai benkyou shimasu ka?
english: How long do you study every day?
exampleRomaji: Mainichi dono kurai benkyou shimasu ka?
japaneseFurigana: 毎(まい)日(にち)どのくらい勉強(べんきょう)しますか？
exampleEn: How long do you study every day?
audioPath: clips/006_毎日どのくらい勉強しますか.wav
grammar2: どのくらい = how long

romaji: Mainichi ichi-jikan benkyou shite imasu.
english: I study for one hour every day.
exampleRomaji: Mainichi ichi-jikan benkyou shite imasu.
japaneseFurigana: 毎(まい)日(にち)一(いち)時(じ)間(かん)勉強(べんきょう)しています。
exampleEn: I study for one hour every day.
audioPath: clips/007_毎日1時間勉強しています。.wav
grammar2: 一(いち)時(じ)間(かん) = one hour

romaji: Subarashii desu ne.
english: That's wonderful, isn't it?
exampleRomaji: Subarashii desu ne.
japaneseFurigana: 素晴(すば)らしいですね。
exampleEn: That's wonderful, isn't it?
audioPath: clips/008_素晴らしいですね。.wav
grammar2: 素晴(すば)らしい = wonderful

romaji: Rainen wa motto muzukashiku naru to omoimasu.
english: I think it will become even more difficult next year.
exampleRomaji: Rainen wa motto muzukashiku naru to omoimasu.
japaneseFurigana: 来(らい)年(ねん)はもっと難(むずか)しくなると思(おも)います。
exampleEn: I think it will become even more difficult next year.
audioPath: clips/009_来年はもっと難しくなると思います。.wav
grammar2: 〜と思(おも)う = I think that...

romaji: Demo, anata nara daijoubu deshou.
english: But I think you'll be fine.
exampleRomaji: Demo, anata nara daijoubu deshou.
japaneseFurigana: でも、あなたなら大(だい)丈(じょう)夫(ぶ)でしょう。
exampleEn: But I think you'll be fine.
audioPath: clips/010_でもあなたなら大丈夫でしょう。.wav
grammar2: 〜でしょう = probably

romaji: Mainichi ganbarimasu.
english: I will do my best every day.
exampleRomaji: Mainichi ganbarimasu.
japaneseFurigana: 毎(まい)日(にち)頑張(がんば)ります。
exampleEn: I will do my best every day.
audioPath: clips/011_毎日頑張ります。.wav
grammar2: 頑(がん)張(ば)る = to do one's best

romaji: Shōrai wa Nihon de hatarakitai desu ka?
english: Do you want to work in Japan in the future?
exampleRomaji: Shōrai wa Nihon de hatarakitai desu ka?
japaneseFurigana: 将来(しょうらい)は日本(にほん)で働(はたら)きたいですか？
exampleEn: Do you want to work in Japan in the future?
audioPath: clips/012_将来は日本で働きたいですか.wav
grammar2: 〜たい = want to do...

romaji: Nihon no kaisha de hatarakitai to omotte imasu.
english: I am thinking of working at a Japanese company in the future.
exampleRomaji: Nihon no kaisha de hatarakitai to omotte imasu.
japaneseFurigana: 日本(にほん)の会(かい)社(しゃ)で働(はたら)きたいと思(おも)っています。
exampleEn: I am thinking of working at a Japanese company in the future.
audioPath: clips/013_日本の会社で働きたいと思っています。.wav
grammar2: 〜と思(おも)っている = am thinking of doing...

romaji: Donna shigoto o shitai desu ka?
english: What kind of job would you like to do?
exampleRomaji: Donna shigoto o shitai desu ka?
japaneseFurigana: どんな仕事(しごと)をしたいですか？
exampleEn: What kind of job would you like to do?
audioPath: clips/014_どんな仕事をしたいですか.wav
grammar2: どんな = what kind of

romaji: Konpyūtā no shigoto o shitai desu.
english: I want to work in a computer-related job.
exampleRomaji: Konpyūtā no shigoto o shitai desu.
japaneseFurigana: コンピューターの仕事(しごと)をしたいです。
exampleEn: I want to work in a computer-related job.
audioPath: clips/015_コンピューターの仕事をしたいです。.wav
grammar2: 仕(し)事(ごと) = job

romaji: Nihon no seikatsu wa tanoshii to omoimasu yo.
english: I think life in Japan is fun.
exampleRomaji: Nihon no seikatsu wa tanoshii to omoimasu yo.
japaneseFurigana: 日本(にほん)の生(せい)活(かつ)は楽(たの)しいと思(おも)いますよ。
exampleEn: I think life in Japan is fun.
audioPath: clips/016_日本の生活は楽しいと思いますよ。.wav
grammar2: 楽(たの)しい (fun) ↔ つまらない (boring)

romaji: Bukka ga takai desu kara, sukoshi shinpai desu.
english: I am a little worried because the cost of living is high.
exampleRomaji: Bukka ga takai desu kara, sukoshi shinpai desu.
japaneseFurigana: 物価(ぶっか)が高(たか)いですから、少(すこ)し心配(しんぱい)です。
exampleEn: I am a little worried because the cost of living is high.
audioPath: clips/017_物価が高いですから少し心配です。.wav
grammar2: 心(しん)配(ぱい)する (to worry) ↔ 安(あん)心(しん)する (to feel relieved)

romaji: Tōkyō wa takai desu ga, hoka no machi wa yasuku narimasu yo.
english: Tokyo is expensive, but other cities become cheaper.
exampleRomaji: Tōkyō wa takai desu ga, hoka no machi wa yasuku narimasu yo.
japaneseFurigana: 東(とう)京(きょう)は高(たか)いですが、他(ほか)の街(まち)は安(やす)くなりますよ。
exampleEn: Tokyo is expensive, but other cities become cheaper.
audioPath: clips/018_東京は高いですが他の街は安くなりますよ。.wav
grammar2: 高(たか)い (expensive) ↔ 安(やす)い (cheap)

romaji: Sore o kiite anshin shimashita.
english: I feel relieved to hear that.
exampleRomaji: Sore o kiite anshin shimashita.
japaneseFurigana: それを聞(き)いて安心(あんしん)しました。
exampleEn: I feel relieved to hear that.
audioPath: clips/019_それを聞いて安心しました。.wav
grammar2: 安(あん)心(しん)する = to feel relieved

romaji: Anata no Nihongo wa motto jōzu ni naru to omoimasu.
english: I think your Japanese will become even better.
exampleRomaji: Anata no Nihongo wa motto jōzu ni naru to omoimasu.
japaneseFurigana: あなたの日本語(にほんご)はもっと上手(じょうず)になると思(おも)います。
exampleEn: I think your Japanese will become even better.
audioPath: clips/020_あなたの日本語はもっと上手になると思います。.wav
grammar2: 上(じょう)手(ず)になる = to become good at

romaji: Arigatou gozaimasu.
english: Thank you very much.
exampleRomaji: Arigatou gozaimasu.
japaneseFurigana: ありがとうございます。
exampleEn: Thank you very much.
audioPath: clips/021_ありがとうございます。.wav

romaji: Mainichi taihen deshou.
english: It must be tough every day.
exampleRomaji: Mainichi taihen deshou.
japaneseFurigana: 毎日(まいにち)大変(たいへん)でしょう。
exampleEn: It must be tough every day.
audioPath: clips/022_毎日大変でしょう。.wav
grammar2: 大(たい)変(へん) (tough) ↔ 楽(らく) (easy)

romaji: Kanji no benkyou mo tanoshiku narimashita.
english: Studying kanji has become fun as well.
exampleRomaji: Kanji no benkyou mo tanoshiku narimashita.
japaneseFurigana: 漢字(かんじ)の勉強(べんきょう)も楽(たの)しくなりました。
exampleEn: Studying kanji has become fun as well.
audioPath: clips/023_漢字の勉強も楽しくなりました。.wav
grammar2: 楽(たの)しくなる = to become fun

romaji: Kore kara mo issho ni ganbarimashou.
english: Let's keep working hard together from now on too.
exampleRomaji: Kore kara mo issho ni ganbarimashou.
japaneseFurigana: これからも一緒(いっしょ)に頑張(がんば)りましょう。
exampleEn: Let's keep working hard together from now on too.
audioPath: clips/024_これからも一緒に頑張りましょう。.wav
grammar2: 頑(がん)張(ば)る = to do one's best
